summary: Target-level refinement of the accepted BSD.8 rational certificate core. It specifies exact finite descent and primary exponent data, a zero-first-layer shortcut, whole-Sha primary assembly, a finite rank-one saturation search, complete local replay, and exact period/height/index transport. These independent inputs identify the actual BSD.5 defect with an exact rational ledger and discharge every exceptional prime before the existing reconstruction theorem is applied. The result is conditional on supplied certificates for the stated curve or family, never a uniform all-prime BSD theorem.

nodes.title: Rational arithmetic ledger
nodes.statement: For a rational a and natural numbers t,s,C, normalizedDefect(a,t,s,C) is a·t²/(s·C), with the natural numbers cast to Q. This is a light arithmetic function, not a definition of elliptic-curve data. In its BSD use a is the proved normalized analytic leading term L*/(Ω Reg_BSD), t is the actual torsion order, s the actual whole-Sha order, and C the actual finite Tamagawa product. The function is total with the field convention at a zero denominator; the arithmetic theorems require a>0 and t,s,C>0.
proofSteps: Compose multiplication, a square and division in Q. No analytic quantity or cohomology group is defined from these scalars.
acceptance: Zero-denominator evaluation is exposed and cannot enter a positive BSD certificate.

nodes.title: Exact valuation balance
nodes.statement: Let p be prime, a be a nonzero rational and t,s,C positive naturals. The integer v_p(normalizedDefect(a,t,s,C)) equals v_p(a)+2v_p(t)−v_p(s)−v_p(C). Consequently it is zero exactly when v_p(a)+2v_p(t)=v_p(s)+v_p(C). All valuations of natural inputs mean their rational casts (equivalently padicValNat cast to Z).
hypotheses: p is prime.
proofSteps: Use nonzero natural casts and padicValRat.mul, .div and .pow. Rearrange the resulting equality in Z.
acceptance: At p=2, a=1,t=2,s=C=1 gives valuation 2. The square is retained.
Negative valuations are allowed; a=1/4,t=s=C=1 gives dyadic valuation −2.

nodes.title: Finite support of the arithmetic ledger
nodes.statement: For a≠0 and t,s,C>0, the canonical prime support of normalizedDefect(a,t,s,C) is contained in S_a∪primeFactors(t)∪primeFactors(s)∪primeFactors(C), where S_a is the accepted Rat.primeSupport(a). Every member of this union is prime. This is a cover, not generally equality: cancellation can remove primes. It supplies a computable support cover once the exact rational a and finite orders are certified; the bad-reduction primes alone are not this cover.
proofSteps: For a prime outside the union each factor has valuation zero by the accepted support characterization and Nat.mem_primeFactors. Apply the valuation balance. Use the accepted equivalence between zero valuation and absence from rational support.
acceptance: a=1/5,t=5,s=1,C=5 has ledger support empty although the cover is {5}.
a=2,t=s=C=1 needs the prime 2 even when a proposed local bad-prime list omits it.

nodes.title: Certified primary descent data
nodes.statement: For an actual E/Q, a prime p, and a proved Mordell–Weil rank r, PrimaryDescentCertificate(E,p,r) consists of: an integer n≥1, m=p^n; a finite additive commutative group F and an additive equivalence F≃Sel_m(E/Q) to the actual cohomological Selmer group; a finite additive group U and equivalence U≃E(Q)_tors; and an independent proof that p^n kills the actual subgroup Sha(E/Q)[p∞]. The Selmer equivalence includes the actual local conditions at every place; a bound on its size or a list of locally soluble candidates without completeness is insufficient. Define k_m=#U[m] and the extracted primaryOrder=#F/(m^r·k_m), using natural division. The order specification and exact divisibility are theorems, not fields. The Kummer maps and rank proof come from the actual E and the imported elliptic-curve theory. No field stores a predicted Sha cardinality or a zero BSD defect.
hypotheses: E/Q is an elliptic curve and r is its proved Mordell–Weil rank.
p is prime; the Mordell–Weil and actual Selmer/Sha carriers are imported.
proofSteps: Use the existing Selmer group, torsion subgroup and AddCommGroup.primaryComponent of the actual Sha group. Store a finite group presentation with an actual equivalence, an exponent and its independent annihilation proof. Define the extracted natural number by the displayed finite cardinalities; establish its specification in primary-order-extraction.
acceptance: The independent exponent proof is checked on Sha[p∞], not just on Sha[p^n].
The definition does not promise that finite descent or an evaluated exponent certificate can be found for every E and p.

nodes.title: Exact order from a certified descent level
nodes.statement: For c:PrimaryDescentCertificate(E,p,r), let m=p^n and k_m=#E(Q)_tors[m]. The subgroup Sha(E/Q)[p∞] is finite and equals Sha(E/Q)[m] inside the actual Sha group. The positive integer D=m^r·k_m divides #F, and #F=D·#Sha[p∞]. Thus c.primaryOrder=#Sha[p∞]>0. The equality uses the actual Kummer sequence, not a rank bound or the predicted BSD order.
hypotheses: The inputs and independent primary exponent proof of primary-descent-certificate.
proofSteps: For m=p^n, Sha[m] is contained in Sha[p∞] by its defining power-killed property; the certificate gives the reverse containment.
The injective Kummer image has cardinality [E(Q):mE(Q)]=m^r·#E(Q)[m] by the pinned Tau Ceti theorem. Identify E(Q)[m] with U[m].
Finite Selmer and Kummer exactness identify the quotient with Sha[m]. Count cosets to get the product equality; D>0 gives divisibility and an exact natural quotient.
acceptance: Finite Selmer alone proves finiteness of Sha[m], not of all Sha[p∞].
For the test #F=16,m=2,r=1,k_m=2, the product equality is 16=4·4.

sources.match: Uses the finite Kummer quotient. Identifying it with the whole primary part is the additional certified-exponent step, not a claim of the source.

nodes.title: A trivial first layer kills the primary subgroup
nodes.statement: For a prime p and actual E/Q of known Mordell–Weil rank r, a complete finite model of Sel_p with cardinality p^r·#E(Q)_tors[p] proves Sha(E/Q)[p]=0 and hence Sha(E/Q)[p∞]=0. This special zero-order producer needs no independent exponent certificate and no prior whole-Sha finiteness. It does require exact rank and equality of the finite Selmer cardinality, rather than an upper bound that has not been matched with the Kummer lower bound.
hypotheses: p is prime.
Actual complete Sel_p model and proved rank r; the displayed cardinality equality.
proofSteps: Count the Kummer quotient as in primary-order-extraction, at m=p, to obtain a trivial Sha[p].

If a nonzero element of Sha[p∞] were killed by p^k, choose a minimal such k; then k≥1 and p^(k−1) times it would be nonzero p-torsion. This contradicts the first step. This is a direct use of the existing primaryComponent, not a new group theory.
acceptance: An E with r=1 and no rational 2-torsion needs #Sel_2=2, not #Sel_2=1.
A first layer of order 4 does not determine a full primary order; the certificate must use primary-order-extraction instead.

sources.match: Exact equality of soluble and locally soluble covering counts makes the first Sha layer vanish. The primary-group consequence follows by taking a minimal power.
Sharpen the accepted warning: nontrivial first layers need an exponent, while a trivial one already annihilates the whole primary part.

nodes.title: Whole Sha order from bounded primary descents
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have analytic rank at most one. Given a positive integer B with a proved annihilation B·Sha(E/Q)=0, put P=primeFactors(B). For each p∈P take a complete finite model F_p≃Sel_{p^n_p}(E/Q), where n_p=v_p(B)≥1, and the actual torsion model U. The annihilator supplies each primary exponent proof, so #Sha(E/Q)=∏_{p∈P}(#F_p/((p^n_p)^r·#U[p^n_p])). Every quotient is exact and positive. For p∉P the primary subgroup is trivial. If B=1, P is empty and Sha is trivial. Existence of an unspecified finite Sha or an unspecified constant d_E is not a supplied B.
hypotheses: The analytic-rank bound and hence actual rank r and finite Sha from BSD.4.
B>0 and a proof that B kills whole Sha over Q.
Complete finite models at precisely the displayed levels and an exact torsion model.
proofSteps: For p|B use coprimality of B/p^n_p with p to show that B-annihilation kills the p-primary subgroup by p^n_p. For p∤B the same Bezout argument kills the entire primary subgroup.

Apply primary-order-extraction at each p. Use the pinned TauCeti.AddCommGroup.primaryDecomposition to identify whole Sha with its primary product. The annihilator makes components outside primeFactors(B) trivial; add the remaining trivial factors if B has extra primes.

If a Kolyvagin bound is used to obtain B, import its evaluated constants with their field and lattice hypotheses; an E/K result requires a proved restriction/corestriction comparison before being used over Q.
acceptance: A bound over an imaginary quadratic field is not directly a bound over Q at p=2.
With B=1 the empty product is 1.
A prime with independently certified trivial first layer can use zero-first-layer-primary-vanishing and omit a deeper computation, without claiming the general nontrivial case is solved.

nodes.title: A finite search certificate for a primitive point
nodes.statement: For an actual E/Q of proved rank one and P∈E(Q) non-torsion, PrimitivePointSearch(E,P) records a real C with a proof h_naive(Q)≤h_BSD(Q)+C for every nonzero affine rational point Q, a natural H≥1 with h_BSD(P)/4+C≤log H, and a finite list L of rational points. Each list entry is verified on E; L includes every affine rational point of naive logarithmic x-height at most log H. For every R∈L it records an exact relation R=k_R P+T_R, k_R∈Z and T_R rational torsion. Completeness can be checked by enumerating reduced coordinates x=a/c², y=b/c³ with c≥1, gcd(a,c)=gcd(b,c)=1 and max(|a|,c²)≤H, solving the integral Weierstrass equation exactly. Identity is handled separately. No field asserts that P generates all rational points.
hypotheses: The model is integral and nonsingular; rank E(Q)=1; P is non-torsion.
h_BSD is the x-height normalization, twice the pinned Tau Ceti canonical height.
proofSteps: Package a proved global height-difference bound and a certified integer search bound. The finite coordinate search verifies points and an exact torsion relation for each listed point. Completeness is only for the bounded set, and is not the desired unbounded generation theorem.
acceptance: The finite list includes every admissible denominator; a point search over integral x alone is insufficient.
An approximate floating relation is replaced by an exact equation in E(Q).

sources.match: The bounded naive-height search certifies a rank-one generator because any missing generator has canonical height at most one quarter of that of a nonprimitive point. The source uses the doubled Silverman height; constants must be transported before use.

nodes.title: Primitive point and regulator from a finite search
nodes.statement: For PrimitivePointSearch(E,P), the image of P generates E(Q)/E(Q)_tors, and Reg_BSD(E/Q)=h_BSD(P)>0. The full index [E(Q):ZP] is the torsion order t, not one unless torsion is trivial. The saturation theorem proves a basis assertion for the free quotient; it does not erase torsion.
hypotheses: A rank-one-search certificate for the actual rank-one E and non-torsion P.
proofSteps: By Mordell–Weil the free quotient is Z. Write P=kQ modulo torsion for a generator Q. If |k|≥2, the quadratic height gives h_BSD(Q)=h_BSD(P)/k²≤h_BSD(P)/4.
The height bound places Q inside the complete finite list. Its recorded relation Q=jP+T gives 1=jk on the free quotient, contradicting |k|≥2. Thus |k|=1.
Apply the accepted height/index comparison and GZ normalization dictionary. The quotient by ZP still contains exactly the rational torsion.
acceptance: The test P=2Q modulo torsion cannot pass.
For a primitive P and torsion order 5, I_free=1 whereas [E(Q):ZP]=5.

nodes.title: Correcting an unsaturated point quotient
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have analytic rank one and let P be non-torsion with proved free index I=[E(Q)/tors:Z·P]>0. If a_P∈Q has real image L′(E,1)/(Ω_E h_BSD(P)), then a=I²a_P has real image L′(E,1)/(Ω_E Reg_BSD(E/Q)). In particular the defect ledger uses normalizedDefect(I²a_P,t,s,C). A primitive-point certificate is the I=1 case. If a full Mordell–Weil index J is supplied, first prove J=I·t and extract I exactly; J² cannot replace I².
hypotheses: Analytic rank one and rank equality.
P is non-torsion and I is its proved free index.
The displayed rational-to-real equality for a_P is exact.
proofSteps: Use h_BSD(P)=I²Reg_BSD from the accepted saturation/index interface. Substitute into the rational-to-real leading quotient.
If P is given as kQ+T relative to a certified primitive Q, prove I=|k| by the rank-one free quotient; the height equality is then the quadratic scaling law.
acceptance: For I=2 and a_P=1/4 the normalized a is 1, not 1/4.
For I=1 and t=5, a full index J=5 must not introduce an extra factor 25.

nodes.title: Replaying the complete Tamagawa product
nodes.statement: Let E have a specified nonsingular integral Weierstrass model with nonzero discriminant Δ. For each prime ℓ dividing |Δ|, a replayed EC Layer-4 Tate trace, including its model transformations and minimality check, identifies a positive integer c_ℓ with [E(Q_ℓ):E₀(Q_ℓ)]. Put C=∏_{ℓ∈primeFactors(|Δ|)}c_ℓ. Then C is the actual finite Tamagawa product of E; outside this finite set the model has good reduction and the factor is one. Nonminimal input models are allowed only when their local transformations are verified. At ℓ=2,3 use the actual small-characteristic branches; additive reduction has its own trace. There is no separately inserted infinite-place factor because Ω_E is the full real period.
hypotheses: An actual integral model with Δ≠0.
A correct Tate trace at every divisor of Δ, not a possibly incomplete list of bad places.
proofSteps: Import correctness of each local trace from EllipticCurves Layer 4, including the identification of the computed integer with the point-group index.
At primes outside the discriminant support use good reduction and c_ℓ=1. Reindex the finite product, allowing extra good primes introduced by a nonminimal integral model.
Use the imported full-real-period convention when feeding C into the arithmetic quotient.
acceptance: At a good extra place the factor is one.
The rational prime 2 may divide c_ℓ at an odd bad ℓ; ledger-support-cover factors C itself, not merely the bad primes.
Doubling Ω for two real components and also adding c_∞ would double count.

sources.locator: §3.2, pp.65–68, Tate algorithm, in particular steps 4–17, 29–31 and 66–78
sources.match: The source distinguishes the small-characteristic branches and computes the local point-group index; the target assembles supplied correct traces without replanning Tate’s algorithm.

nodes.title: Exact period and height transport
nodes.statement: Let Ω_B,R_B be nonzero real BSD period and regulator, r∈{0,1}, and u,v∈Q be nonzero with Ω_src=u·Ω_B and R_src=v^r·R_B under the canonical real embedding. If a_src is rational and casts to L*/(Ω_src R_src), then a_B=u·v^r·a_src casts to L*/(Ω_B R_B). For every prime p and a_src≠0, v_p(a_B)=v_p(a_src)+v_p(u)+r v_p(v). For the pinned Tau Ceti regulator v=1/2 since Reg_BSD=2^r Reg_Tau. When Ω_src is the identity-component real period and E(R) has two components, u=1/2. These powers of two are exact; an odd p-unit comparison cannot certify p=2.
hypotheses: All displayed real equalities are proved for the actual chosen differential and height normalization.
Ω_B,R_B,u,v and a_src are nonzero where valuations are used.
r=0 or r=1.
proofSteps: Substitute the exact period and regulator scalings and cancel nonzero denominators in R.
Use padicValRat multiplication and power for the valuation statement. The GZ.0 dictionary fixes which direction the factor 2 takes.
acceptance: At r=1,u=1,v=1/2,a_src=2 the corrected a_B is 1 and the dyadic valuation drops by one.
At r=0 the regulator correction is v^0=1.
If both u and v are 1/2 at r=1, the correction is 1/4.

sources.match: The source explicitly uses a doubled Silverman height. The exact pinned Tau Ceti comparison is imported from GZ.0, rather than inferred from a height name.
These fix full real period and BSD regulator conventions for the actual defect.

nodes.title: Identifying the actual BSD defect with the ledger
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have analytic rank r≤1 with the BSD.4 rank equality and whole-Sha finiteness. Let t=#E(Q)_tors>0, let s>0 be the exact whole-Sha order obtained from certified primary data or another proved finite equivalence, and let C>0 be the complete local product. Suppose a∈Q>0 has proved real image L*(E,1)/(Ω_E Reg_BSD(E/Q)), with the full real period and BSD height normalization. Then BSD.5’s actual bsdDefect(E)=normalizedDefect(a,t,s,C) in Q. For rank one a may be obtained from point-normalized-leading-quotient and leading-quotient-normalization. For rank zero the regulator is one. Numerical recognition of a, an analytic predicted value of s, or an unsaturated point does not satisfy these premises.

nodes.title: Completing the exceptional-prime certificate
nodes.statement: For an actual E/Q of analytic rank ≤1, assume the equality d_E=normalizedDefect(a,t,s,C) of arithmetic-data-identifies-defect and a finite set S of primes. Suppose every prime p outside S has a proved source-qualified equality v_p(d_E)=0, and for every p∈S the exact integer balance v_p(a)+2v_p(t)=v_p(s)+v_p(C) is certified. Construct the accepted Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate(d_E), using its constructor from exceptions. Alternatively, take S to be the explicit union in ledger-support-cover; then the outside-S proof follows from the ledger itself. This supplies full BSD for precisely this E. An indexed family requires these same data and all prime proofs for every member, not a uniform sufficiently-large-prime assertion.

gaps.title: Evaluated nontrivial-primary certificates for individual curves
gaps.detail: The plan determines the exact certificate contract and proves its conditional order theorem. It does not obtain a numerical whole-Sha bound for arbitrary E/Q from finiteness. HE.7/exceptional-primary-sha-bound has actual imaginary-quadratic, non-CM, quotient and integral constants; these must be evaluated and transported to Q with all kernels before it can provide the primaryExponent field. At a prime with zero first layer the zero-first-layer theorem avoids this input. Concrete nontrivial-primary producers remain an explicit arithmetic obligation, never a database prediction.
